questions.question: What does a red flashing traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A red flashing light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop. Then you may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs warn you of no passing zones. The sign will also have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and keep going through the intersection.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light, slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If stopping is not safe, proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road with oncoming traffic, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to complete your pass. Only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, you should:
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, glance over the shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Know that tinted windows make it harder to see at night.
Carry a flashlight in your car.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights causes your eyes to adjust. After the car passes, your eyes need time to readjust to darker light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: You are charged with driving under the influence and refuse a chemical test. Your license can be suspended for 12 months:

options.text: Only if you are convicted of driving under the influence.
Only if you are convicted of a traffic violation.

questions.explanation: When you drive, you agree to take a chemical test if a police officer asks. If you refuse the test, your license will be suspended for at least one year.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign shows:

options.text: A speed that can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
A recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed advisory signs on curves and turns show a recommended speed for that area. Even if you can go faster in good weather, never exceed the recommended speed in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to freeway speed so you can merge smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point downward, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you see this hand signal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to keep to the right to avoid a driving hazard ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle downhill on a two-way street:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the side of the road when parking downhill. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.

questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, like vehicles striping roads or removing snow. They are marked with orange signs with black letters or symbols. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, you should first:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
questions.explanation: First, pull up next to the car in front of your parking space. Check traffic and signal before turning your wheels to park.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Driving with your headlights out of alignment because one side of your car is higher than the other.
Damaging a tire from drifting onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning, if the shoulder has water on it.
Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops off the road onto a low shoulder, do not brake hard or steer sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Pentagonal signs indicate:
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs show you are in a school zone. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change when driving on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Other cars are often hidden in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets, or five seconds before on freeways.

questions.question: A speed limit sign is posted on a freeway exit ramp. You should:

options.text: Slow to this speed before entering the deceleration lane.
Regard the posted limit as only a suggestion.
Never drive slower than the posted speed on the exit ramp.
Slow to the posted speed once entering the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to the posted speed once entering the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed steady until you are on the exit ramp. Then slow down smoothly to the posted speed limit.

questions.question: When towing a trailer, you must make sure that:

options.text: The trailer has a safety chain securely attached to the trailer hitch.
The trailer has a safety chain securely attached to the vehicle's bumper.
The trailer has a safety chain securely attached to the frame of the towing vehicle.
The trailer hitch is equipped with a fail-safe latch.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer has a safety chain securely attached to the frame of the towing vehicle.
questions.explanation: Safety chains must connect the trailer to the frame of your vehicle. Do not attach them to the hitch or bumper.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel too far in the other direction.
Turn your steering wheel toward the traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction the skid is moving.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction the skid is moving.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to skid, stay calm. Steer the wheel in the direction the skid is moving.

questions.question: When towing a trailer, how much of the trailer's total weight should rest on the vehicle's hitch?
questions.explanation: About 10 to 15 percent of the trailer's weight should be on the vehicle's hitch. If the weight is not balanced correctly, you will have trouble controlling the vehicle or trailer.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that matches the current road conditions.

questions.explanation: You must drive at a reasonable and safe speed. Consider the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and lighting. Always follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes dangerous gases from your vehicle and keeps them out of the passenger area. Fix any exhaust leaks right away to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you of an upcoming railroad crossing. Slow down and be extra careful at these locations.

questions.question: You are waiting at an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another vehicle hits you from behind, this prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. Signal, look for an opening in traffic, speed up to match traffic speed, and merge into a safe opening.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road hazards. This sign tells you that a stop sign is coming up and you should prepare to stop completely.
